- Overestimate prices when sentiment is positive and recent highs are followed by a spike — model tends to overshoot and fail to correct downward.
- Underestimate prices when sentiment is negative or neutral, especially after a sharp drop — model fails to recognize mean reversion or risk-off behavior.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term sentiment swings, particularly when sentiment peaks or dips sharply — adjust forecast by dampening volatility in high-sentiment periods.
- When sentiment is low or negative, model often fails to anticipate downward drift — apply a downward bias correction for 3–5 days after negative sentiment spikes.
- Forecast tends to lag in correcting for recent price declines — especially when sentiment is weak, model holds onto prior highs longer than true market behavior.
- In high-sentiment periods, model often overestimates the duration of the trend — reduce forecast slope or add early correction if sentiment turns negative within 3–5 days.
- When sentiment is mixed or volatile, model tends to average out extremes — consider using sentiment-weighted smoothing or adjusting for sentiment volatility index.
